reel.caption:
PPF deposit after the 5th: why can it cost you ₹888 a year?

PPF interest is worked out each month on the lowest balance between the 5th and the month-end.
Money that arrives after the 5th earns nothing for that month.
Illustrative ₹1.5 lakh a year at 7.1% (the current rate): deposited by 5 April ≈ ₹10,650 of interest; after 5 April only 11 months count ≈ ₹9,763. About ₹888 less.
Paying ₹12,500 monthly? Missing the 5th every month adds up to about the same.
Simple interest for clarity; PPF compounds yearly, so actual credits differ slightly.

Do you deposit in April, or a little every month?

Sources: a business news site on Oct–Dec 2026 small-savings rates (PPF 7.1%, 30 Sep 2026); the same site on the 5th-of-month rule (Apr 2026); a national daily's PPF explainer with a ₹887.50 one-month example. Illustrative only.
